project.title: Karbala Awareness Platform
project.label: Case Study / Educational Platform
project.subtitle: An Arabic-first educational season that turns thirteen nights of content into a navigable, measurable learning experience.
project.metaDescription: The Karbala source describes a Next.js platform with public content, timed quizzes, quiz analytics, visitor analytics, an admin dashboard, and a managed Supabase gallery.

sections.title: The idea looked simple
paragraphs: A content season can be published as a set of pages, but that does not make it feel like a journey.
sections.primaryImage: Opening scene that establishes the product tension

sections.title: The experience the product needed
paragraphs: The product goal was to let visitors browse the season, explore all nights, read content, access resources, listen to recordings, view cards, and participate in timed quizzes while administrators manage the material.
sections.primaryImage: Target user journey or primary product surface

sections.title: The constraint underneath
paragraphs: Arabic-first, RTL-first, mobile-first content must remain readable while quiz timing, grading, media, and admin operations stay trustworthy.

sections.title: A credible first model
paragraphs: The project combines Next.js App Router routes, Supabase PostgreSQL/Auth/Storage, public content components, quiz state, analytics, and an admin surface for the season's data.

sections.title: The friction of real use
paragraphs: The documented system has to protect quiz answers until submission, enforce schedule and late-submit rules, manage gallery storage, and recover once from stale deployment chunks.
sections.primaryImage: Broken state, issue capture, or boundary case

sections.title: The reasonable fixes that needed revision
paragraphs: The documented system has to protect quiz answers until submission, enforce schedule and late-submit rules, manage gallery storage, and recover once from stale deployment chunks.

sections.title: The deeper system problem
paragraphs: The platform became more than a content site when each public interaction needed a corresponding state, policy, or operational workflow.

sections.title: Rebuilding the boundaries
paragraphs: The source separates public routes, admin routes, API routes, Supabase migrations and RLS, storage helpers, quiz components, and shared types so content operations do not leak into the learner experience.

sections.title: Product quality under real conditions
paragraphs: The documented deployment process explicitly treats standalone static assets as part of runtime correctness; missing them can cause ChunkLoadError or 404s.
sections.primaryImage: Scoped benchmark, test evidence, or reliability check

sections.title: What emerged
paragraphs: The result is a public season experience with nights, cards, resources, quizzes, gallery, and an admin dashboard for managing the same content.

sections.title: What changed and what remains open
paragraphs: Karbala is best presented as a structured educational product whose trust comes from content flow, quiz safeguards, analytics, and operational control—not only from its visual theme.
